section_summary: This section opens with Joseph C. Grew’s despatch transmitting the complete English translation of Japan’s 1938 National General Mobilization Law, which authorized sweeping wartime controls over labor, industry, trade, finance, property, publications and military production. It is followed by duplicate intelligence reports on Major General Aketo Nakamura and a report on Japanese Army promotions, reserve placements and assignments to fortresses and military schools. The section ends with a file note cross-referencing a Chinese protest against extending the mobilization law to Japan’s mandated Pacific islands.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 2871 Transmitting the National General Mobilization Law
subfiles.doc_type: diplomatic despatch with translated legal enclosure
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Transmits the Embassy's English translation of Japan's National General Mobilization Law, Law No. 55 of 1938.
subfiles.summary: The despatch encloses the law as passed by the Imperial Diet, promulgated on March 31, 1938, and published on April 1. Its fifty articles authorize extensive wartime control of labor, industrial production, trade, finance, transportation, property, prices, technical training, research and publications. It establishes enforcement mechanisms, compensation rules, criminal penalties and a National General Mobilization Deliberative Commission, while repealing the Military Munitions Industry Mobilization Law.

subfiles.title: Report No. 9342: Major General Aketo Nakamura
subfiles.about: Profiles Major General Aketo Nakamura following his appointment as Director of the War Department's Military Affairs Bureau.
subfiles.summary: Report No. 9342 on Major General Aketo Nakamura: career from the Military Academy through staff and Manchukuo service, named April 14, 1938 to replace Machijiri, a logical choice with no particular specialty.

subfiles.title: Charge Slip for File 894.20
subfiles.about: Records the charging of file 894.20 to E. L. Van Oss.
subfiles.summary: Charge slip for decimal file 894.20 dated October 12, 1940.

subfiles.title: Duplicate of Report No. 9342: Major General Aketo Nakamura
subfiles.about: Duplicates the biographical intelligence report on Major General Aketo Nakamura and his new Military Affairs Bureau appointment.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate of Report No. 9342 on Major General Nakamura: career record, selection to succeed Machijiri, and his leadership of the Women's National Defense Association in Manchuria.

subfiles.title: Report No. 9344: March Promotions and Assignments
subfiles.about: Reports Japanese Army promotions, reserve placements, attaché transfers and senior assignments announced during March 1938.
subfiles.summary: The report tabulates promotions by rank and branch and names officers promoted to senior rank. It also records first-reserve placements, the relief of military attaché Kumakichi Harada, and appointments to fortress commands, military schools, the Army Staff College, the Army Remount Department, the Army Arsenal and the Kwantung Army. Japanese press commentary welcomed the changes as favoring younger officers, revitalizing military education and preparing the Army for modern equipment and prolonged hostilities.

subfiles.title: Document File Note on the Application of the Mobilization Law to Pacific Mandated Islands
subfiles.about: Cross-references a Geneva telegram concerning China's protest against application of Japan's mobilization law to the Japanese-mandated Pacific islands.
subfiles.summary: File note on telegram no. 122: China protested to the League Secretary-General about extending Japan's May 1938 mobilization law to the mandated Pacific islands.
